selection_policy.episode_format: one practical original story about one source-supported idea, not a full-book recap
selection_policy.diversity: prefer a different book than the most recent episode; never repeat same lesson until eligible pool exhausted

lessons.topic: Why making a habit easier beats waiting for motivation
lessons.claim: James Clear describes making a desired response easy as one of the four laws of behavior change.
lessons.visual_action: Host prepares a notebook on the desk and makes the first step simpler
lessons.hook_angle: The reason you skip your habit might be the friction, not your willpower

lessons.topic: Shrink a new habit to its first two minutes
lessons.claim: James Clear recommends scaling a new habit down to a version that takes less than two minutes to begin.
lessons.visual_action: Host changes a large reading goal to opening a book and reading one page
lessons.hook_angle: Try making the first step laughably small

lessons.topic: Change your environment to make your next good choice easier
lessons.claim: Clear's four laws include making the cue for a desired behavior obvious.
lessons.visual_action: Host moves a notebook into plain view and places a distracting phone away
lessons.hook_angle: You can change a habit before you feel motivated

lessons.topic: Why deep focus is more valuable than frantic multitasking
lessons.claim: Cal Newport defines deep work as focusing without distraction on cognitively demanding tasks.
lessons.visual_action: Host silences phone, closes extra tabs and works on one demanding idea
lessons.hook_angle: Busy is not the same as focused

lessons.topic: Give deep work a protected time slot
lessons.claim: Newport describes time blocking and depth rituals as strategies for making room for deep work.
lessons.visual_action: Host blocks out a focused work session in a calendar then starts work
lessons.hook_angle: Don't wait for an empty calendar to find focus

lessons.topic: Money decisions are emotional, not only mathematical
lessons.claim: The publisher describes the book as exploring how behavior and personal history shape money decisions.
lessons.visual_action: Host compares two everyday spending decisions at a kitchen table without inventing financial results
lessons.hook_angle: Two people can see the same numbers and decide differently
